missed_issues: The 'prompt+code is not significantly different from code-only' result (§VI-A) carries the most useful practical implication and the review states the stat but does not surface it: once the test generator sees the implementation, also giving it the spec does not recover oracle quality, so the fix is to isolate the test step from the code entirely, not to add the spec alongside it.

The fault dataset keeps only the single hardest faulty implementation per task (fails the fewest reference tests, <=50%), so the absolute detection rates (the abstract's 14%/25%) reflect deliberately hard-to-detect faults; the robust takeaway is the within-pair direction (code exposure drags detection down), not the absolute levels. The review flagged unreported N but not that the hardest-fault selection shapes the headline percentages.

On the contamination point the review raises: memorization of HumanEval+/MBPP would raise both arms (the model knows the canonical behavior from the spec either way), so it mainly inflates absolute oracle quality, not the differential between spec-only and code-exposed arms, which is what the paper isolates; the effect also persists on the less-memorized BigCodeBench, so contamination weakens the magnitude more than the direction.
note: I agree with admit_with_caveats, COI none, relevance 4, and every pattern stance, including the two supports: P15/P14 are backed by a genuine isolating comparison (same 5 models, same faulty implementations, same LLM-Plain loop; only whether the test step sees the code varies), significant 5/5, and the P36/P37 tags are correctly held to neutral because only a two-turn chat is measured, not a workflow graph vs a loop. The review is sharper than my blind pass: it caught that the number of faulty implementations behind every p-value is never reported, that Mann-Whitney ignores the paired design with no multiple-comparison correction, the contamination risk, and that prior work [5]/[7] already showed explicit code exposure biases oracles (only the implicit-conversation RQ3 is new). Those justify its rigor 3 over my blind 4, reproducibility 1 over my 2 (nothing of theirs is released), and generalizability 2 over my 3 (Python function-level only); the merge takes the lower in each case and I concur.
